resolutions.title: The shared fence tracker misreads a fence nested in a list item, so an example inside one now counts as a task

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: Feed createFenceTracker the line with its leading whitespace stripped in both parseCheckboxes and parseTouchpoints, so a fence at any indent opens and closes by character and length; add the list-nested case (and the four-backtick case) to both parsers' tests, and say in design D4 why these two readers strip indent.

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Keep CommonMark's 0-3 indent rule and name the list-nested fence as a limit in design D4 (and a residual the size requirement does not state), accepting that an example nested in a task item reads as tasks.

resolutions.action: applied the ratified direction A in parseCheckboxes: the shared tracker is fed each line with its leading whitespace stripped, so an example nested under a task item at 4+ spaces is fenced and a four-backtick fence still closes only on its own length (tests: the reproduction plus a sibling task after it, and a nested four-backtick fence holding a three-backtick line). Pushback partially applied for the Touchpoints half: a mutation check showed its nested case is unobservable — every line inside a 4+-space fence is indented, so it can never match the `## ` heading or a top-level entry, and indented bullets are skipped — so the strip was reverted there (it would only let an indented code block swallow entries) and its test pins that reasoning. Design D4 states which reader strips and why.
